headline: GXAI and GOOG take the biggest hits today as AI stocks broadly sell off, while oil surges nearly 3% on warnings of multi-decade low inventories.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The Global X AI ETF was the hardest hit in today's session, falling 4.6%. This ETF holds the big AI-linked tech names, and broader tech sold off sharply — the NASDAQ dropped over 1% last night. Any wobble in AI sentiment flows straight into this ETF.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG dropped 2% last night in what was a rough session for big tech. Despite solid fundamentals — analysts are pointing to Google's growing cloud backlog and strong Search cash flows — the market broadly rotated away from AI-heavy names. Still up 22.9% overall on your buy-in price.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL fell 1.96% today despite oil actually rising — WTI crude jumped nearly 3% last night after the US EIA warned global crude inventories are heading toward multi-decade lows. The ASX lag means today's close didn't yet capture that tailwind. Watch for a bounce tomorrow.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara fell another 1.71% today, continuing its soft run — you're now down 14.5% on your position. Lithium sector commentary is mixed: some analysts are flagging a supply shift and quiet revival, while others note the broader ASX 200 lithium reset. No strong near-term catalyst in sight.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.97% today. Emerging markets have been under some pressure with the US dollar holding firm and global risk appetite soft. No specific catalyst today — just the broader 'risk-off' mood dragging the sector.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO dipped 0.61% last night. The GTA 6 hype cycle continues — there's chatter about a potential third trailer dropping soon and debate about the map size — but the stock is drifting slightly as investors wait for concrete release news. Down 9.1% on your buy-in.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged down 0.39% last night — a relatively mild move compared to the broader tech selloff. The AI-driven cloud momentum story remains intact; the slight dip looks more like general market softness than any MSFT-specific problem. Down 9.3% on your entry price.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.31% today, tracking overnight US market weakness from the NASDAQ/S&P sell-off. Your overall position is essentially flat on cost — just $0.35 in the green. Holds steady as a diversified US market bet.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today — down just 0.08%. Its diversified mix of Australian and international shares acted as a buffer against the broader tech sell-off. Essentially flat on your invested amount.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — worst mover in the portfolio today
watch_today.detail: Down 4.6% today and now 10.6% below your buy-in. The Global X AI ETF is highly sensitive to NASDAQ swings, and with the NASDAQ down over 1% last night and AI sentiment wobbly, this could stay under pressure. No specific news triggered today's drop — it's macro-driven. Hold for now unless the thesis on AI growth has changed for you.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — could bounce tomorrow, oil up nearly 3% overnight
watch_today.detail: FUEL dropped 1.96% today on the ASX, but here's the thing: crude oil surged 2.98% last night to $90.83/barrel after the US Energy Information Administration warned that global oil inventories are heading toward multi-decade lows. The ASX close didn't price that in yet. Watch for a bounce at tomorrow's open — the underlying macro is turning more favourable.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — still drifting, no strong catalyst yet
watch_today.detail: Pilbara is down 14.5% on your entry and slipped another 1.71% today. The lithium sector is in a quiet recovery phase — analysts are talking about improving demand and low-cost supply advantages — but there's no near-term price trigger. Hold if you believe in the longer-term EV/battery story, but be aware it may stay soft for a while.

watch_today.title: GOOG — solid fundamentals, short-term tech headwinds
watch_today.detail: GOOG fell 2% last night but is still 22.9% above your entry price — your best performing position. Analysts are flagging Alphabet's growing cloud backlog and its dominant Search cash engine as key strengths that outlast the AI spending debate. The dip looks like broad tech weakness rather than anything Google-specific. Hold comfortably.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision — watch for cut signal this week
watch_today.detail: Multiple economists and news outlets today are warning the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) must cut interest rates soon or risk tipping Australia into a recession. There's growing consensus that the next move will be a cut, not a hike. A rate cut is generally good for growth assets like shares and property. Keep an eye on any RBA statement or economic data this week — it could move your ASX holdings.

watch_today.title: Gold falls 2.8% — risk-off but not in the usual way
watch_today.detail: Gold dropped $119 to $4,141/oz last night, which is unusual — typically gold rises when stocks fall. The simultaneous drop in stocks AND gold suggests investors may be selling assets broadly to raise cash, or rotating into something specific. Oil spiking while gold and stocks fall is worth watching as a signal that inflation fears may be resurfacing.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was rough for tech — the NASDAQ fell 1.09% and the S&P 500 dropped 0.86%, dragging most of your US holdings lower. The big story is oil: crude surged nearly 3% to $90.83 a barrel after the US Energy Information Administration (the government body that tracks energy supply) warned inventories are heading to multi-decade lows — that means oil stocks could get a boost. Gold had an unusual bad day, dropping 2.8% to $4,141, despite the broader market weakness. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to 70.2 US cents, which softens the impact of your US holdings when converted back to AUD.

politics.summary: Today's Australian political news is dominated by one topic: whether the Reserve Bank needs to cut interest rates urgently to prevent a recession. Multiple economists, publications and analysts have weighed in today — and the consensus is shifting clearly toward a cut.

stories.title: Reserve Bank warned it must cut rates or risk triggering a recession
stories.why_it_matters: Economists are now openly warning that the RBA risks causing a recession if it doesn't start cutting interest rates soon. The argument is straightforward: with household budgets squeezed by high borrowing costs and economic growth slowing, leaving rates too high for too long could push Australia into negative growth territory. For homeowners and anyone with a variable-rate mortgage, a rate cut would mean lower monthly repayments. For investors, lower rates generally lift share prices and property values.

stories.title: Experts agree: RBA's next move will likely be a rate cut, not a hike
stories.why_it_matters: A broad sweep of market economists now believe the RBA's next move will be a rate cut rather than another hike — a significant shift in thinking from earlier this year. This is important for your portfolio: rate cuts tend to be good for growth assets like shares and ETFs, as cheaper borrowing encourages business investment and lifts asset prices. It also boosts consumer confidence, which flows through to the broader economy.

stories.title: Fears Reserve Bank won't be able to cut rates even in a recession
stories.why_it_matters: A more concerning angle emerging today: some analysts worry the RBA may be stuck — if inflation stays sticky (i.e. prices keep rising even as the economy slows), the bank may not be able to cut rates even if we do tip into a recession. This 'stagflation' scenario — slow growth plus persistent inflation — would be the worst outcome for households and investors alike. It's not the base case, but it's a real tail risk worth watching.

stories.title: Has the RBA Finally Finished Raising Interest Rates?
stories.why_it_matters: Property analysts are joining the chorus, suggesting the RBA rate hike cycle is over. If correct, this is meaningful for Gold Coast property values — the end of rate rises typically stabilises or re-inflates house prices. For your growth ETFs like VDHG, the end of rate hikes removes a key headwind that has weighed on valuations over the past two years.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Anthropic releasing Claude Fable 5 to the general public — a powerful new model that brings their previously exclusive 'Mythos' technology to everyday users. There's also fresh noise about upcoming model releases from OpenAI and Google, and regulatory pressure is building globally.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 — its most powerful publicly available model ever
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic has publicly launched Claude Fable 5, bringing the underlying technology from its previously private 'Mythos' model — which reportedly shook Wall Street two months ago when it was quietly rolled out — to the general public. In plain terms, this is Anthropic's most capable AI assistant available to anyone. It's also available on Snowflake's enterprise platform (Cortex AI), meaning businesses can start using it in their data workflows immediately. This is directly competitive with GPT and Gemini.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: A new executive order from the Trump administration is set to change the process by which AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic can release new AI models to the public. The details are still emerging, but it signals that even the Trump White House — which has been broadly pro-tech — is starting to impose some guardrails on AI rollouts. For your GOOG and MSFT holdings, new regulatory hurdles could slow product launches or add compliance costs.

stories.title: Australia's AI regulation set for crucial review
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's approach to regulating artificial intelligence is up for a major review. Currently, Australia has a relatively light-touch approach — no dedicated AI law like the EU's. The review will determine whether Australia needs stricter rules around things like AI transparency, safety testing, and liability. For Australian investors in AI ETFs like GXAI.AX, tighter local rules could affect the operating environment for any Australian AI businesses in the fund.

stories.title: ComfyUI builds a tool that pits OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Moonshot AI against each other
stories.why_it_matters: ComfyUI — a popular open-source AI tool used by image and video creators — has released a system that automatically sends code review tasks (called 'pull requests') to multiple AI models at once: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Moonshot AI. It then lets you compare their answers side-by-side. In practical terms, this makes it easier for developers to pick the best AI for each job, which is good for AI adoption broadly — but also intensifies the competition between the major AI labs.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 kicks off tomorrow night with Rabbitohs vs Broncos, and there's a sentimental story around South Sydney ahead of the match. AFL's Big Freeze drew record interest, Gary Ablett gets a Hall of Fame nod, and Nick Kyrgios is making noise at a major tournament.

stories.title: Souths to honour Jake Arrow with white jersey against the Broncos
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney will wear a white jersey tomorrow night against Brisbane at Accor Stadium to honour Jake Arrow, in what looks to be a tribute match ahead of Round 15. It adds an emotional backdrop to what is already a big South Sydney-Broncos derby. Kick-off is 7:50 PM Thursday.

stories.title: Wayne's big Latrell update and Round 15 team news
stories.why_it_matters: Wayne Bennett has given a significant update on Latrell Mitchell's availability heading into Round 15, and there's also news about a debutant for South Sydney. Madge (Jason Demetriou) has also addressed selection calls around Liam Mam. Key team news to know before Thursday's Rabbitohs-Broncos game — check confirmed lineups before locking in your tips.

stories.title: AFL Big Freeze draws brilliance and drama — Neale Daniher tribute
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's annual Big Freeze at the MCG — the charity event where coaches and footy personalities slide into an ice bath to raise money for MND research, in honour of Neale Daniher — drew strong crowds and high emotion this year. The Guardian described it as a night of 'drama, brilliance and freewheeling footy.' AFL also announced record crowds and viewership for Round 13, showing the competition is in rude health.

stories.title: Gary Ablett inducted into AFL Hall of Fame
stories.why_it_matters: Gary Ablett — widely considered one of the greatest AFL players of all time — has been officially inducted into the AFL Hall of Fame. His Geelong teammates have paid tribute, and the football world is celebrating the recognition of a five-time premiership player (across both clubs) with 495 games to his name. A well-deserved honour for a true legend of the game.

stories.title: Kyrgios 'emotional' after beating a seed in sizzling comeback win
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios described himself as 'emotional' after knocking out a seeded opponent in what reporters called a sizzling comeback win. The result continues Kyrgios's resurgent form at the current tournament — a rare moment of composure and quality from a player whose fitness and commitment have often been in question. Aussie tennis fans will be watching closely as he progresses.
